title: How to find actual good music
author: _RaXeD
selftext:
Hello guys, I'm kind of in a pickle... Of all the things I would expect to find as a roadblock when creating a game, I didn't expect sound to be the one I can't seem to solve.

I thought I had planned for it by using only old songs and public-domain background tracks, but how wrong I was...

I didn't know copyright needs like 100 years to expire. I wanted to use Mr. Sandman as an intro song, it would fit my setting perfectly, a 1954 song, I thought, who would care... Long story short, it might be copyrighted until 2070.

But fine, I will just use what is available in the public domain... Turns out 98% of it is crap, and there really isn't an easy way to find the gems, you just have to listen to song after song, hoping that something that doesn't even match what you are looking for but just resembles it pops up.

There is also AI as a solution. I played with a few generators for a bit, and the results were good, far above what is available in the public domain. But it's AI. I don't mind using AI, especially for music. I can't feel sympathetic to any big label that got its 100+ year-old protected song stolen. But what would players think? Would they even notice? And if they do notice, would they care? I'm trying to make something high-quality, and I feel that AI music (despite being honestly good) would somehow stain that.

Has anyone solved this? Is there like a hidden oasis of good free songs somewhere that I have not found? Perhaps an easy way to find public domain gems? Is everyone using AI in their games already, and I'm overthinking not wanting to use it?

comments.author: k4b0b
comments.body:
The options in order of increasing effort/cost:
1. Asset store music
2. AI generated (Suno)
3. Use the AI generated tracks as inspiration, create your own with a DAW, or remix using the stems
4. Hire someone to do #3

Are you using AI generated assets for your visuals? The concept is the same for music. If you take it as-is, artifacts will be noticeable to keen observers. Fine for prototyping but you’ll have to clean it up for a finished game.

Plus, AI music is super apparent; you can't really claim it as your own even if you edit it, but anyway, thank you for the suggestions!

comments.author: reynoldsmkatie
comments.body:
This is the biggest annoyance for me in gene dev too! Same for making reels about my game for Instagram or TikTok. I spend ages finding a good song, buy it off iTunes, put in on my reel, then upload it to social media only to have TikTok strip out my audio until I change the music to some royalty free crap that doesn’t fit what I’m looking for. Or YouTube just blocked my video altogether.

I would pay for it too if I knew how! Like how do you get licensed to put the songs you want in your game or videos? Do you have to pay for a full commercial license the same way a real corporation would if they wanted to use a certain song in a tv commercial? That seems like overkill when I’m just making a silly little video for my one hundred followers. I haaate looking for music!

replies.author: _RaXeD
replies.body:
There are virtually zero chances of being able to get rights to post popular songs. Unless you are ready to pay 1-2k minimum. The music industry is brutal and kind of disgusting.  
  
There are some subscription services, like [envato.com](http://envato.com), for example, that allow you to post songs from their catalog on social media.

The quality is just a notch above what is available in the public domain, don't expect anything crazy.

This is why I made this post, I'm also looking for any kind of solutions to this.

comments.author: xcdesz
comments.body:
Did you try Humble Bundle?  Every few months they offer a giant bundle of pretty decent royalty free audio and music assets.   Certainly good enough for indie game development. 

Or you could even buy a DAW like Fruity Loops and delve into the audio track generation rabbit hole yourself, with some creativity.  Its actually a pretty fun hobby to take up..  

Or just use an AI generator like Suno.. there is even a local generator call Ace Step that you can run on a PC with a decent GPU.  

There are so many options its mind blowing.

But if you really want something beautiful, you will need to pay an actual musician if you want something that meets a high standard.  A professional game company would hire a musician or multiple musicians, or contract this out.  The musicians are also likely to be using all of the above options that I mentioned, in addition to actual physical instruments.

As an indie developer you need to prioritize what matters most.  Even with AI out there, you still need to be in control making these decisions.  Making a publishable game is not going to be a one click experience.

replies.author: _RaXeD
replies.body:
I'm not looking for a one-click experience; I have already embraced the hell I'm about to enter. I just didn't expect music to be so heavily gatekept. I understand how important a good track is; some are even responsible for the game's success in one way or another, yet they treat music like it's made of gold.

We can use software that costs millions to make, just by promising to pay back IF our game is a success, but god forbid we want to use a track from 1954...

I did check Humble Bundle amongst 20 other websites, but sadly, I'm looking for a western/blues post apocalyptic asthetic, and they don't seem to have anything like that. All I mostly found were no lyric songs made for commercials.

Learning to make my own music is not really an option; I know basically nothing, and when combined with how complex game dev is, I can't really afford to go down that rabbit hole if I want the game to release this decade.

I will just use AI... It's leagues better than what you can find for free or even from subscription services like Envato. It can basically do 85% of what a real artist can do. I don't like the option, but it's the only one I have with my current budget if I want to avoid putting elevator music in my game.

I would honestly happily pay if there was a fair subscription out there, something that didn't cost too much and had actual songs. I can't pay Universal Music Publishing $2k+ in order to use actual music.

comments.author: burgric
comments.body: Composer here. Been developing a game for a while now and the soundtrack is one of the main elements I am really looking forward to implementing. Like any art form I suppose AI can only synthesise an imitation. If you want a soundtrack unique to your project that induces the desired emotional experience you want your players to have, I believe hiring a composer is the only way you can achieve that. The collaboration between dev and composer, in my experience, is symbiotic and very rewarding. And it'll make your game shine. What I really need is a 3D artist. Meshy is OK but it's a slog to get it right. Anyway, hope this helps
